fieldMarks: Ears small relative to other cottontails.
Head and back a mix of dark brown, rusty brown or black; throat, belly and tail white.
Clear cinnamon-coloured ring around the eye.
behavior: Most active at dawn, dusk and night; hides motionless by day in hollow logs or dense grass.
Flees in a zig-zag and will enter water, staying still with only its nose above the surface.
Eats grasses, sedges, shrubs, bark, seedlings and twigs.
Usually silent except when threatened; males scent-mark territories.
habitat: Swampy lowlands, marshes, floodplains, river tributaries and cypress swamps, usually close to water; rests in depressions in tall grass or leaves.
range: South-central United States and the Gulf Coast, abundant in Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana, and also in parts of South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Oklahoma and Missouri. Not found in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Eastern cottontail
lookalikes.howToTell: The swamp rabbit is the largest cottontail, with relatively small ears and a clear cinnamon eye-ring.
